text: Friston: — PRS-CANDIDATE-01 is the technical basis for the trace-blankets-subsume-Markov-blankets claim (CROSS-032). The generalization from acyclic to cyclic graphs lives here.

Wolfram: — Observer-restricted effective dynamics from a larger substrate is structurally the same move as Wolfram's observer-dependent coarse-graining of the ruliad. Both make the observer's computational boundedness constitutive of the physics it sees. Existing wiki entry CROSS-033 touches this; the primary paper strengthens it.
Arkani-Hamed: — Feeds the positive-geometry bridge (CROSS-033), though the concrete associahedron claim belongs to the whitepaper's Conjecture 7, not this paper.

Hawkins: — Worth noting as a genuine structural rhyme: a trace kernel is a complete-but-partial model built by an observer with restricted access, which is formally close to what a cortical column is in Thousand Brains Theory. Hawkins grounds this biologically and stays agnostic on ontology; Hoffman grounds it ontologically and treats the biology as interface. The productive tension already record

Friston: — Strongest signal in the document. RTL is presented as an assumption-weaker generalization of active inference, citing Parr, Pezzulo & Friston (2022) directly. This *extends* existing CROSS-032 (trace blankets subsume Markov blankets): the whitepaper now makes the subsumption claim about the *inference dynamics*, not only the boundary structure. Recommend the Friston agent be dispatched

Arkani-Hamed: — Conjecture 7 names ABHY associahedra as subpolytopes of the Markov polytope, and §5.4 explicitly proposes integrating **surfaceology** (Arkani-Hamed et al. 2025, *JHEP*) with RTL. This is the most concrete form the amplituhedron-derivation bridge has taken; the wiki has carried it as "Speculative" since the RC Pilot.

Carroll: — Direct contact with the standing productive tension. The whitepaper insists it does not abandon physics but proposes recovering known laws as limiting cases. Conjectures 1-2 (recovering Minkowski and curved spacetime) are precisely what Carroll's poetic naturalism would demand before taking the program seriously; they are now on the record as commitments.

Kastrup: — §2 and §5.3 give a non-dual ontology reached by mathematical rather than argumentative route; the whitepaper cites Chalmers' "realist idealist" positioning. Convergence with analytic idealism, different derivation — consistent with the existing dispatch.

Levin: — §5.2 raises "the possible existence of conscious agents and their traces external to the brain, including questions about the potential ubiquity of consciousness in nature." Extends CROSS-034.

Hawkins: — Weak but real: the "microchip epistemology" section diagnoses deep learning's inefficiency and proposes a non-standard architecture. Hawkins reaches a similar diagnosis from the opposite ontology (resolutely biological). Worth flagging as a *productive tension* rather than convergence — same target, incompatible grounds.

Stump: — §5.3's free-will discussion explicitly contrasts Christian voluntarist traditions (probabilities as ontic manifestation of free will) with Madhyamaka Buddhist readings (probabilities as principled unpredictability). This is a direct, named invitation to the Thomistic tradition, and the framework leaves the question open rather than settling it.
